title: Offering his book to the archives and writers
summary: He offers his book and photos to the Institute and complains about writers.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: So I'm hoping, if you'd like to, sometime in the near future, I may ask you to, when these things are in the archives, that you may include my book as a supplement to them. It's on the house. I'm making you a gratis offer. And included with that would be the pictures that are going to be in my book. And possibly an appeal to the black musician to wake up. What do you think?
How can it be done? How can this be the supplement to what you already have?
The thing would be how do you bring it to the attention of the musicians.

You're right about it. You re right about it. That's... I think you wrote a review...you wrote an article for me once, Dan, in Downbeat. I don't remember whether you wrote it or whether you got it together and we never got together on it. But what we need, we need some writers. See, the Major Robbs(?) and those guys, they don't write a goddamn thing, them son of a bitches, they write, but it's not what we need. And then, too, I can't blame them, because they don't know, they don't have...they may not have the same ideas that I have. They may not have the same feel!ng. If you like Count Basie and that's it, you know. And they like Duke and that's it. But what about the future? What about posterity? What about the lineage? What about history?
Well, what you said earlier about going into the school system and getting to the kids. Letting them know about it, that's very, very important.
Did I get your support in that?
But I mean in how it works.
Let me come up with the schematic, okay? Let me come up...

There / a lady in Washington not too long ago that was head of a get-together organized by Radio Free Jazz Magazine and she had an idea about the curriculum, you know, on black music for the schools, for elementary schools. And, you know...
And she gave me some stuff on paper. I'd like you to look at it...
